title: Unleashing the Potential of AQFP Logic Placement via Entanglement Entropy and Projection
problem: In AQFP circuits, signal attenuation with increasing wirelength causes data errors, requiring rows of buffers as repeaters for synchronization. These inserted buffers significantly amplify power consumption and circuit delay.
motivation: AQFP logic offers superior energy efficiency compared to traditional RSFQ logic and has emerged as a prominent superconductor-based logic family.
method: The framework uses entanglement entropy to initialize circuit topology, guiding placement decisions to minimize buffer insertion. It then applies projection-based techniques for placement and buffering, avoiding computationally intensive Lagrangian optimization while ensuring data synchronization across AC-powered clock phases.
key_novelty: Applying entanglement entropy for topology initialization and projection-based placement to minimize buffer insertion in AQFP circuits without expensive optimization.
contributions: Entanglement entropy-based topology initialization for AQFP placement
81% average reduction in required buffer rows
1.88x acceleration in processing time versus state-of-the-art
